Path homology of a digraph with phlite_grpph

Grounded persistent path homology (GrPPH) tells apart cycles that an undirected method would treat alike: a long directed cycle lives longer than a short one, a square of two parallel paths dies quickly, and a bidirected edge is a small loop of its own. We build a digraph with a few of each, compute its barcode with representatives, and highlight them.

data.text/markdown: Four H1 bars, all born at 0 (in the grounded filtration the graph's own edges are there from the start), with very different lifetimes: the bidirected edge dies at 0.5, its weight; the two paths from c3 to t2, which are not a directed cycle, at 1; the directed 4-cycle at 2 and the directed 6-cycle at 3. A directed cycle of ||(n||) unit edges lives until ||(n / 2||). Each representative is a list of edges:

Watching the filtration

In the grounded filtration the graph's own edges are there from the start, and at time ||(t||) a new edge ||(u \to v||) appears (dashed) once the shortest path from ||(u||) to ||(v||) has length at most ||(t||). Cycles are filled in by longer paths through the digraph. The bidirected edge's loop and the two parallel paths die (at 0.5 and 1) before any new edge appears: paths along the graph's own edges are enough to fill them. The directed 4- and 6-cycles need the new edges, and die at 2 and 3. On the right, the bars alive at ||(t||) are highlighted.
